    94→## 20260217 - Fix: test race condition with `std::env::set_var` / `remove_var`
    95→
    96→### Problem
    97→
    98→`tspec test` intermittently failed on the `resolve_spec_path_none_with_env` test in
    99→`tspec-build`. The failure was not reproducible when running `tspec test -p tspec-build`
   100→alone — only when both packages ran together via `tspec test`.
   101→
   102→### Root cause
   103→
   104→Rust runs tests in parallel on multiple threads within the same process.
   105→`std::env::set_var()` and `std::env::remove_var()` are process-wide — they mutate
   106→shared global state. Two tests that manipulate the same env var (`TSPEC_SPEC_FILE`)
   107→race each other:
   108→
   109→- `resolve_spec_path_none_with_env` — sets `TSPEC_SPEC_FILE`, calls function, removes it
   110→- `resolve_spec_path_none_without_env` — removes `TSPEC_SPEC_FILE`, asserts `None`
   111→
   112→If the "without" test runs between the set and remove of the "with" test, it sees the
   113→var and fails. Or vice versa. This is a well-known Rust testing pitfall — `set_var` is
   114→marked `unsafe` in Rust 2024 edition precisely because of this.
   115→
   116→### Solutions considered
   117→
   118→1. **Static Mutex** — wrap env-var tests so they run one at a time. Works but easy to
   119→   forget for new tests, and doesn't prevent the class of bug.
   120→2. **`serial_test` crate** — adds `#[serial]` attribute. Clean syntax but adds a
   121→   dependency and still relies on developers remembering to annotate.
   122→3. **`--test-threads=1`** — heavy-handed, slows down all tests.
   123→4. **`_inner` pattern (chosen)** — extract a pure function that takes env values as
   124→   parameters. The public function reads env vars and delegates. Tests call `_inner`
   125→   directly with their own values — no shared state, no race, impossible to flake.
   126→5. **Temp directory copies (for future integration tests)** — when tests need to
   127→   modify real package layouts (Cargo.toml, spec files, source), each test copies
   128→   the fixture into its own `tempdir()`. No shared filesystem state, parallel-safe,
   129→   cleanup is automatic via `Drop`.
   130→
   131→### Principle
   132→
   133→Push side effects (env var reads, file I/O) to the edges. Keep core logic pure and
   134→parameterized. Tests exercise the logic without touching the real world. For filesystem
   135→mutations, each test owns a private copy.
   136→
   137→### Changes
   138→
   139→- **tspec-build/src/lib.rs:** Split `resolve_spec_path` into a thin env-reading wrapper
   140→  and `resolve_spec_path_inner` that takes `manifest_dir` and `env_spec_file` as
   141→  `Option<&str>` parameters. Rewrote all three `resolve_spec_path_*` tests and
   142→  `emit_from_reads_spec_file` to call `_inner` directly — no `set_var`/`remove_var`.
   143→
   144→### Status
   145→
   146→Done.
   147→
   148→## 20260217 - Refactor cargo runner functions into unified fn
   149→
   150→### Context
   151→
   152→Three functions share nearly identical structure:
   153→- `cargo_build::build_package` — builds with optional spec, returns `BuildResult`
   154→- `testing::test_package` — tests with optional spec, returns `()`
   155→- `cargo_build::plain_cargo_build_release` — builds without spec, returns `BuildResult`
   156→
   157→They all follow the same skeleton: find workspace/package/tspec, clean stale build.rs,
   158→optionally load spec, generate build.rs if needed, construct `Command` (with optional
   159→`+nightly`), run, clean up, warn about stale files.
   160→
   161→`plain_cargo_build_release` is just `build_package` with `tspec=None` and `release=true`.
   162→`test_package` differs only in the subcommand (`test` vs `build`) and has its own
   163→duplicate `requires_nightly()` function in `testing.rs`.
   164→
   165→### Plan
   166→
   167→Unify into a single `run_cargo` function that takes the subcommand as a parameter.
   168→`plain_cargo_build_release` becomes a thin call. `test_package` becomes a wrapper that
   169→calls the unified function and discards `BuildResult`. The duplicate `requires_nightly()`
   170→in `testing.rs` is eliminated.
   171→
   172→### Differences to reconcile
   173→
   174→| Aspect | `build_package` | `test_package` | `plain_cargo_build_release` |
   175→|---|---|---|---|
   176→| Subcommand | `build` | `test` | `build` |
   177→| Spec | optional | optional | never |
   178→| Returns | `BuildResult` | `()` | `BuildResult` |
   179→| `+nightly` | via `build_cargo_command()` | inlined `requires_nightly()` | no (no spec) |
   180→| build.rs gen | yes (checks bin target) | yes (no bin check) | no |
   181→
   182→### Status
   183→
   184→Not started.
   185→
   186→## 20260217 - Remove `[rustc]` section, promote `build_std`, add `rustflags`
   187→
   188→### Context
   189→
   190→The `[rustc]` section has two remaining fields: `build_std` (actually a cargo `-Z` flag,
   191→not a rustc flag) and `flags` (raw RUSTFLAGS passthrough). `build_std` belongs under
   192→`[cargo]` since it triggers `+nightly` and `-Z build-std=...`. `flags` becomes a
   193→top-level `rustflags` array — a simple escape hatch mirroring `RUSTFLAGS` semantics.
   194→
   195→### Before → After
   196→
   197→```toml
   198→# Before
   199→[rustc]
   200→build_std = ["core", "alloc"]
   201→flags = ["-C", "some-thing"]
   202→
   203→# After
   204→[cargo]
   205→build_std = ["core", "alloc"]
   206→
   207→rustflags = ["-C", "some-thing"]
   208→```
   209→
   210→### Changes
   211→
   212→1. **types.rs:** Move `build_std` to `CargoConfig`, add `rustflags` to `Spec`, delete `RustcConfig`
   213→2. **cargo_build.rs:** Update all `spec.rustc` references to new locations
   214→3. **testing.rs:** Update duplicate `requires_nightly()` to use `spec.cargo.build_std`
   215→4. **ts_cmd/edit.rs:** Update field registry and tests
   216→5. **ts_cmd/set.rs, unset.rs:** Update tests
   217→6. **tspec.rs:** Update tests (remove `RustcConfig` references)
   218→7. **tests/tspec_test.rs:** Update integration tests
   219→8. **README.md, CLAUDE.md:** Update documentation
   220→
   221→### Status
   222→
   223→Done — released in v0.11.6. Also renamed `config_key_value` to `config` with nested table support (dev2).
   224→
```

  "new_string": "Done — released in v0.11.6. Also renamed `config_key_value` to `config` with nested table support (dev2).\n\n## 20260218 - Add custom profile support\n\n### Context\n\nCurrently `cargo.profile` only accepts `\"debug\"` or `\"release\"` (a Rust enum). Cargo supports\ncustom profiles defined in `Cargo.toml` (e.g., `[profile.release-small]` with `inherits = \"release\"`),\nselected via `cargo build --profile <name>`. tspec should support selecting and overriding these\ncustom profiles.\n\nKey insight: Custom profile **definitions** must live in `Cargo.toml` (cargo requirement — they\nneed `inherits`). tspec's role is **selecting** a profile and **overriding** its settings via\n`cargo.config`.\n\nCargo's profile-to-directory mapping: `dev` → `target/debug/`, `release` → `target/release/`,\ncustom → `target/<name>/`.\n\n### Plan\n\nMulti-step (`-devN` series), version `0.12.0`.\n\n**Step 1 (dev1):** Core type change — replace `Profile` enum with `String`, update command\ngeneration (`\"debug\"`/`\"dev\"` → no flag, anything else → `--profile <name>`), update path\nresolution (`profile_dir_name()` helper), relax validation.\n\n**Step 2 (dev2):** CLI `--profile <name>` flag on build/run/test commands, thread through\ncall chain, replace `release: bool` with `Option<String>`.\n\n**Step 3:** Final release — remove `-dev` suffix.\n\n### Status\n\nIn progress."
}

  "new_string": "/// Flatten nested config into dotted key-value pairs for --config args."
}

  "old_string": "/// Get binary path for a build with a spec\npub fn get_binary_path(\n    workspace: &Path,\n    crate_name: &str,\n    spec: &Spec,\n    release: bool,\n    expanded_target_dir: Option<&str>,\n) -> PathBuf {\n    let is_release = release || spec.cargo.profile.as_ref() == Some(&Profile::Release);\n\n    let target = spec.cargo.target_triple.clone().or_else(|| {\n        spec.cargo\n            .target_json\n            .as_ref()\n            .and_then(|p| p.file_stem().map(|s| s.to_string_lossy().to_string()))\n    });\n\n    let profile_dir = if is_release { \"release\" } else { \"debug\" };\n\n    let base = match expanded_target_dir {\n        Some(td) => workspace.join(\"target\").join(td),\n        None => workspace.join(\"target\"),\n    };\n\n    match target {\n        Some(t) => base.join(t).join(profile_dir).join(crate_name),\n        None => base.join(profile_dir).join(crate_name),\n    }\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Get binary path for a build with a spec\npub fn get_binary_path(\n    workspace: &Path,\n    crate_name: &str,\n    spec: &Spec,\n    release: bool,\n    expanded_target_dir: Option<&str>,\n) -> PathBuf {\n    let target = spec.cargo.target_triple.clone().or_else(|| {\n        spec.cargo\n            .target_json\n            .as_ref()\n            .and_then(|p| p.file_stem().map(|s| s.to_string_lossy().to_string()))\n    });\n\n    // Determine profile directory: spec profile takes precedence, then release flag\n    let dir = match spec.cargo.profile.as_deref() {\n        Some(p) => profile_dir_name(p),\n        None => {\n            if release {\n                \"release\"\n            } else {\n                \"debug\"\n            }\n        }\n    };\n\n    let base = match expanded_target_dir {\n        Some(td) => workspace.join(\"target\").join(td),\n        None => workspace.join(\"target\"),\n    };\n\n    match target {\n        Some(t) => base.join(t).join(dir).join(crate_name),\n        None => base.join(dir).join(crate_name),\n    }\n}"
}

  "old_string": "/// Get binary path for a build with a spec\npub fn get_binary_path(\n    workspace: &Path,\n    crate_name: &str,\n    spec: &Spec,\n    release: bool,\n    expanded_target_dir: Option<&str>,\n) -> PathBuf {\n    let target = spec.cargo.target_triple.clone().or_else(|| {\n        spec.cargo\n            .target_json\n            .as_ref()\n            .and_then(|p| p.file_stem().map(|s| s.to_string_lossy().to_string()))\n    });\n\n    // Determine profile directory: spec profile takes precedence, then release flag\n    let dir = match spec.cargo.profile.as_deref() {\n        Some(p) => profile_dir_name(p),\n        None => {\n            if release {\n                \"release\"\n            } else {\n                \"debug\"\n            }\n        }\n    };\n\n    let base = match expanded_target_dir {\n        Some(td) => workspace.join(\"target\").join(td),\n        None => workspace.join(\"target\"),\n    };\n\n    match target {\n        Some(t) => base.join(t).join(dir).join(crate_name),\n        None => base.join(dir).join(crate_name),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Get binary path for a simple build (no spec)\npub fn get_binary_path_simple(workspace: &Path, crate_name: &str, release: bool) -> PathBuf {\n    let profile_dir = if release { \"release\" } else { \"debug\" };\n    workspace.join(\"target\").join(profile_dir).join(crate_name)\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Get binary path for a build with a spec.\n/// `cli_profile` is the CLI-specified profile (None = debug default).\npub fn get_binary_path(\n    workspace: &Path,\n    crate_name: &str,\n    spec: &Spec,\n    cli_profile: Option<&str>,\n    expanded_target_dir: Option<&str>,\n) -> PathBuf {\n    let target = spec.cargo.target_triple.clone().or_else(|| {\n        spec.cargo\n            .target_json\n            .as_ref()\n            .and_then(|p| p.file_stem().map(|s| s.to_string_lossy().to_string()))\n    });\n\n    // Determine profile directory: spec profile takes precedence, then CLI profile\n    let dir = match spec.cargo.profile.as_deref() {\n        Some(p) => profile_dir_name(p),\n        None => match cli_profile {\n            Some(p) => profile_dir_name(p),\n            None => \"debug\",\n        },\n    };\n\n    let base = match expanded_target_dir {\n        Some(td) => workspace.join(\"target\").join(td),\n        None => workspace.join(\"target\"),\n    };\n\n    match target {\n        Some(t) => base.join(t).join(dir).join(crate_name),\n        None => base.join(dir).join(crate_name),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Get binary path for a simple build (no spec).\n/// `cli_profile` is the CLI-specified profile (None = debug default).\npub fn get_binary_path_simple(\n    workspace: &Path,\n    crate_name: &str,\n    cli_profile: Option<&str>,\n) -> PathBuf {\n    let dir = match cli_profile {\n        Some(p) => profile_dir_name(p),\n        None => \"debug\",\n    };\n    workspace.join(\"target\").join(dir).join(crate_name)\n}"
}

Each package uses its own tspecs.\"\n                    );\n                }\n                let workspace = WorkspaceInfo::discover()?;\n                let results = test_all(&workspace, None, cli_profile, self.fail_fast);\n                Ok(print_test_summary(&results))\n            }\n            Some(name) => {\n                if self.tspec.is_empty() {\n                    test_package(&name, None, cli_profile)?;\n                } else {\n                    let package_dir = resolve_package_dir(project_root, Some(&name))?;\n                    let pkg_name = get_package_name(&package_dir)?;\n                    let spec_paths = find_tspecs(&package_dir, &self.tspec)?;\n                    for spec_path in &spec_paths {\n                        let spec_str = spec_path.to_string_lossy();\n                        test_package(&pkg_name, Some(&spec_str), cli_profile)?;\n                    }\n                }\n                Ok(ExitCode::SUCCESS)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}"

    14→const TSPEC_BUILD_RS_MARKER: &str = "// Generated by tspec - do not edit";
    15→pub fn warn_stale_build_rs(had_stale: bool) {
    16→    if had_stale {
    17→        println!("Warning: a stale build.rs was deleted, likely from a previous interrupted build");
    18→    }
    19→}
    20→
    21→/// Check if a build.rs file was generated by tspec.
    22→/// Matches either the marker comment or a file that only contains
    23→/// `cargo:rustc-link-arg-bin=` println lines (marker-less variant).
    24→fn is_tspec_generated_build_rs(content: &str) -> bool {
    25→    if content.starts_with(TSPEC_BUILD_RS_MARKER) {
    26→        return true;
    27→    }
    28→    // Fallback: file only contains fn main, cargo:rustc-link-arg-bin printlns, and braces
    29→    let dominated_by_link_args = content
    30→        .lines()
    31→        .map(|l| l.trim())
    32→        .filter(|l| !l.is_empty())
    33→        .all(|l| {
    34→            l == "fn main() {"
    35→                || l == "}"
    36→                || l.starts_with(TSPEC_BUILD_RS_MARKER)
    37→                || l.contains("cargo:rustc-link-arg-bin=")
    38→        });
    39→    dominated_by_link_args && content.contains("cargo:rustc-link-arg-bin=")
    40→}
    41→
    42→/// Remove a stale tspec-generated build.rs left behind by an interrupted build.
    43→/// Returns true if a stale file was removed. Caller should print a warning after the build.
    44→pub fn remove_stale_tspec_build_rs(pkg_dir: &Path) -> bool {
    45→    let build_rs = pkg_dir.join("build.rs");
    46→    if let Ok(content) = fs::read_to_string(&build_rs)
    47→        && is_tspec_generated_build_rs(&content)
    48→    {
    49→        let _ = fs::remove_file(&build_rs);
    50→        return true;
    51→    }
    52→    false
    53→}

    59→    pub target_base: PathBuf,

    61→
    62→/// Build a package with a spec, returns the binary path on success.
    63→/// `cli_profile` is the profile from the CLI (e.g., "release", "release-small").
    64→/// `None` means debug (default). `Some("release")` is equivalent to `--release`.
    65→pub fn build_package(
    66→    pkg_name: &str,
    67→    tspec: Option<&str>,
    68→    cli_profile: Option<&str>,
    69→) -> Result<BuildResult> {
    70→    let workspace = find_project_root()?;
    71→    let pkg_dir = find_package_dir(&workspace, pkg_name)?;
    72→    let tspec_path = find_tspec(&pkg_dir, tspec)?;
    73→
    74→    // Resolve actual package name from Cargo.toml (needed when pkg_name is a path)
    75→    let pkg_name = get_package_name(&pkg_dir)?;
    76→
    77→    // Clean up any stale tspec-generated build.rs from interrupted builds
    78→    let had_stale_build_rs = remove_stale_tspec_build_rs(&pkg_dir);
    79→
    80→    // Track if we generated a build.rs
    81→    let build_rs_path = pkg_dir.join("build.rs");
    82→    let had_build_rs = build_rs_path.exists();
    83→
    84→    // Load spec once (if present) and compute target_dir
    85→    let (spec, expanded_td) = if let Some(path) = &tspec_path {
    86→        let s = load_spec(path)?;
    87→        let name = spec_name_from_path(path);
    88→        let td = expand_target_dir(&s, &name)?;
    89→        (Some(s), td)
    90→    } else {
    91→        (None, None)
    92→    };
    93→
    94→    // Compute paths
    95→    let target_base = match &expanded_td {
    96→        Some(td) => workspace.join("target").join(td),
    97→        None => workspace.join("target"),
    98→    };
    99→    let binary_path = if let Some(spec) = &spec {
   100→        get_binary_path(
   101→            &workspace,
   102→            &pkg_name,
   103→            spec,
   104→            cli_profile,
   105→            expanded_td.as_deref(),
   106→        )
   107→    } else {
   108→        get_binary_path_simple(&workspace, &pkg_name, cli_profile)
   109→    };
   110→
   111→    // Apply spec if present, otherwise plain cargo build
   112→    let status = if let Some(spec) = &spec {
   113→        let path = tspec_path.as_ref().unwrap();
   114→        println!("Building {} with spec {}", pkg_name, path.display());
   115→
   116→        // Generate temporary build.rs for linker flags if needed
   117→        let has_linker_args = !spec.linker.args.is_empty();
   118→        let has_bin_target = pkg_dir.join("src/main.rs").exists();
   119→        if has_linker_args && !has_bin_target {
   120→            println!(
   121→                "Warning: linker.args ignored for {} (no binary target)",
   122→                pkg_name
   123→            );
   124→        }
   125→        if has_linker_args && has_bin_target && !had_build_rs {
   126→            generate_build_rs(&build_rs_path, &pkg_name, spec)?;
   127→        }
   128→
   129→        let mut cmd = build_cargo_command(spec)?;
   130→        cmd.arg("build");
   131→        cmd.arg("-p").arg(&pkg_name);
   132→        cmd.current_dir(&workspace);
   133→
   134→        // Set spec path for tspec-build library to read in build.rs
   135→        cmd.env("TSPEC_SPEC_FILE", path.as_os_str());
   136→
   137→        apply_spec_to_command(
   138→            &mut cmd,
   139→            spec,
   140→            &workspace,
   141→            cli_profile,
   142→            expanded_td.as_deref(),
   143→        )?;
   144→        cmd.status().context("failed to run cargo")?
   145→    } else {
   146→        println!("Building {} (no tspec)", pkg_name);
   147→        let mut cmd = Command::new("cargo");
   148→        cmd.arg("build");
   149→        cmd.arg("-p").arg(&pkg_name);
   150→        cmd.current_dir(&workspace);
   151→        if let Some(p) = cli_profile {
   152→            match p {
   153→                "debug" | "dev" => {}
   154→                _ => {
   155→                    cmd.arg("--profile").arg(p);
   156→                }
   157→            }
   158→        }
   159→        cmd.status().context("failed to run cargo")?
   160→    };
   161→
   162→    // Clean up generated build.rs (only if we created it)
   163→    if !had_build_rs && build_rs_path.exists() {
   164→        let _ = fs::remove_file(&build_rs_path);
   165→    }
   166→
   167→    if !status.success() {
   168→        bail!("cargo build failed");
   169→    }
   170→
   171→    println!("  {}", binary_path.display());
   172→    warn_stale_build_rs(had_stale_build_rs);
   173→    Ok(BuildResult {
   174→        binary_path,
   175→        target_base,
   176→    })
   177→}
   178→
   179→/// Plain `cargo build --release` with no spec lookup.
   180→/// Used by compare to produce a baseline build.
   181→pub fn plain_cargo_build_release(pkg_name: &str) -> Result<BuildResult> {
   182→    build_package(pkg_name, None, Some("release"))
   183→}
   184→
   185→/// Generate a temporary build.rs with scoped linker flags from tspec.toml
   186→pub fn generate_build_rs(path: &Path, crate_name: &str, spec: &Spec) -> Result<()> {
   187→    let mut lines = vec![TSPEC_BUILD_RS_MARKER.to_string(), "fn main() {".to_string()];
   188→
   189→    for arg in &spec.linker.args {
   190→        lines.push(format!(
   191→            "    println!(\"cargo:rustc-link-arg-bin={}={}\");",
   192→            crate_name, arg
   193→        ));
   194→    }
   195→
   196→    lines.push("}".to_string());
   197→    fs::write(path, lines.join("\n")).context("failed to write build.rs")?;
   198→    Ok(())
   199→}
   200→
   201→/// Check if spec requires nightly toolchain
   202→fn requires_nightly(spec: &Spec) -> bool {
   203→    // High-level panic mode may require nightly
   204→    let panic_needs_nightly = spec.panic.map(|p| p.requires_nightly()).unwrap_or(false);
   205→
   206→    // BuildStd requires nightly
   207→    let has_build_std = !spec.cargo.build_std.is_empty();
   208→
   209→    // Unstable cargo flags require nightly
   210→    let has_unstable = !spec.cargo.unstable.is_empty();
   211→
   212→    panic_needs_nightly || has_build_std || has_unstable
   213→}
   214→
   215→/// Build the base cargo command (with toolchain if needed)
   216→fn build_cargo_command(spec: &Spec) -> Result<Command> {
   217→    let mut cmd = Command::new("cargo");
   218→
   219→    if requires_nightly(spec) {
   220→        cmd.arg("+nightly");
   221→    }
   222→
   223→    Ok(cmd)
   224→}
   225→
   226→/// Apply spec parameters to a cargo command.
   227→/// `cli_profile` is the CLI-specified profile (None = debug default).
   228→pub fn apply_spec_to_command(
   229→    cmd: &mut Command,
   230→    spec: &Spec,
   231→    workspace: &Path,
   232→    cli_profile: Option<&str>,
   233→    expanded_target_dir: Option<&str>,
   234→) -> Result<()> {
   235→    // Set custom target directory if specified
   236→    if let Some(td) = expanded_target_dir {
   237→        cmd.arg("--target-dir")
   238→            .arg(workspace.join("target").join(td));
   239→    }
   240→
   241→    // Handle high-level panic mode (cargo -Z flag)
   242→    if let Some(panic_mode) = spec.panic
   243→        && let Some(z_flag) = panic_mode.cargo_z_flag()
   244→    {
   245→        cmd.arg("-Z").arg(z_flag);
   246→    }
   247→
   248→    // Handle cargo config
   249→    let has_profile = spec.cargo.profile.is_some();
   250→    if let Some(ref profile) = spec.cargo.profile {
   251→        match profile.as_str() {
   252→            "debug" | "dev" => {
   253→                // Debug/dev is default, no flag needed
   254→            }
   255→            _ => {
   256→                cmd.arg("--profile").arg(profile);
   257→            }
   258→        }
   259→    }
   260→
   261→    if let Some(ref triple) = spec.cargo.target_triple {
   262→        cmd.arg("--target").arg(triple);
   263→    }
   264→
   265→    if let Some(ref path) = spec.cargo.target_json {
   266→        cmd.arg("-Z").arg("json-target-spec");
   267→        cmd.arg("--target").arg(path);
   268→    }
   269→
   270→    for flag in &spec.cargo.unstable {
   271→        cmd.arg("-Z").arg(flag);
   272→    }
   273→
   274→    // Inject --config key=value pairs (flattened from potentially nested config)
   275→    for (key, value) in flatten_config(&spec.cargo.config) {
   276→        cmd.arg("--config").arg(format!("{}={}", key, value));
   277→    }
   278→
   279→    // If no profile in spec, fall back to CLI profile
   280→    if !has_profile && let Some(p) = cli_profile {
   281→        match p {
   282→            "debug" | "dev" => {} // default, no flag needed
   283→            _ => {
   284→                cmd.arg("--profile").arg(p);
   285→            }
   286→        }
   287→    }
   288→
   289→    // Collect rustc flags
   290→    let mut rustc_flags: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
   291→
   292→    // Handle high-level panic mode (rustc -C flag)
   293→    if let Some(panic_mode) = spec.panic
   294→        && let Some(panic_value) = panic_mode.rustc_panic_value()
   295→    {
   296→        rustc_flags.push(format!("-C panic={}", panic_value));
   297→    }
   298→
   299→    // Handle high-level strip mode
   300→    if let Some(strip_mode) = spec.strip
   301→        && let Some(strip_value) = strip_mode.rustc_strip_value()
   302→    {
   303→        rustc_flags.push(format!("-C strip={}", strip_value));
   304→    }
   305→
   306→    if !spec.cargo.build_std.is_empty() {
   307→        // -Z build-std is a cargo flag, not rustc
   308→        let crates_str = spec.cargo.build_std.join(",");
   309→        cmd.arg("-Z").arg(format!("build-std={}", crates_str));
   310→    }
   311→
   312→    for flag in &spec.rustflags {
   313→        rustc_flags.push(flag.clone());
   314→    }
   315→
   316→    // Handle version script (generates file and adds linker arg)
   317→    if let Some(vs) = &spec.linker.version_script {
   318→        let vs_dir = match expanded_target_dir {
   319→            Some(td) => workspace.join("target").join(td),
   320→            None => workspace.join("target"),
   321→        };
   322→        let _ = fs::create_dir_all(&vs_dir);
   323→        let version_script_path = vs_dir.join("tspec-version.script");
   324→
   325→        // Generate version script: { global: sym1; sym2; local: *; };
   326→        let globals = vs.global.join("; ");
   327→        let content = format!("{{ global: {}; local: {}; }};", globals, vs.local);
   328→
   329→        let mut f =
   330→            fs::File::create(&version_script_path).context("failed to create version script")?;
   331→        writeln!(f, "{}", content)?;
   332→
   333→        rustc_flags.push(format!(
   334→            "-C link-arg=-Wl,--version-script={}",
   335→            version_script_path.display()
   336→        ));
   337→    }
   338→
   339→    // Apply rustc flags (linker args from Args handled by generated build.rs)
   340→    if !rustc_flags.is_empty() {
   341→        cmd.env("RUSTFLAGS", rustc_flags.join(" "));
   342→    }
   343→
   344→    Ok(())
   345→}

Custom profiles must be defined with \\\n         `[profile.{}]` and an `inherits` field (e.g., `inherits = \\\"release\\\"`).\",\n        profile,\n        cargo_toml_path.display(),\n        profile,\n    )\n}"
}

    11→/// Check if spec requires nightly toolchain
    12→fn requires_nightly(spec: &crate::types::Spec) -> bool {
    13→    // High-level panic mode may require nightly
    14→    let panic_needs_nightly = spec.panic.map(|p| p.requires_nightly()).unwrap_or(false);
    15→
    16→    let has_build_std = !spec.cargo.build_std.is_empty();
    17→
    18→    let has_unstable = !spec.cargo.unstable.is_empty();
    19→
    20→    panic_needs_nightly || has_build_std || has_unstable
    21→}
    22→
    23→/// Test a package with a spec.
    24→/// `cli_profile` is the CLI-specified profile (None = debug default).
    25→pub fn test_package(pkg_name: &str, tspec: Option<&str>, cli_profile: Option<&str>) -> Result<()> {
    26→    let workspace = find_project_root()?;
    27→    let pkg_dir = find_package_dir(&workspace, pkg_name)?;
    28→    let tspec_path = find_tspec(&pkg_dir, tspec)?;
    29→
    30→    // Resolve actual package name from Cargo.toml (needed when pkg_name is a path)
    31→    let pkg_name = get_package_name(&pkg_dir)?;
    32→
    33→    // Clean up any stale tspec-generated build.rs from interrupted builds
    34→    let had_stale_build_rs = remove_stale_tspec_build_rs(&pkg_dir);
    35→
    36→    // Track if we generated a build.rs
    37→    let build_rs_path = pkg_dir.join("build.rs");
    38→    let had_build_rs = build_rs_path.exists();
    39→
    40→    // Validate the effective profile before invoking cargo
    41→    // (need to peek at the spec to check its profile)
    42→    if let Some(path) = &tspec_path {
    43→        let spec = load_spec(path)?;
    44→        let effective = spec.cargo.profile.as_deref().or(cli_profile);
    45→        if let Some(profile) = effective {
    46→            validate_profile(profile, &workspace)?;
    47→        }
    48→    } else if let Some(profile) = cli_profile {
    49→        validate_profile(profile, &workspace)?;
    50→    }
    51→
    52→    // Apply spec if present, otherwise plain cargo test
    53→    let status = if let Some(path) = &tspec_path {
    54→        let spec = load_spec(path)?;
    55→        let spec_name = spec_name_from_path(path);
    56→        let expanded_td = expand_target_dir(&spec, &spec_name)?;
    57→        println!("Testing {} with spec {}", pkg_name, path.display());
    58→
    59→        // Generate temporary build.rs for linker flags if needed
    60→        let has_linker_args = !spec.linker.args.is_empty();
    61→        if has_linker_args && !had_build_rs {
    62→            generate_build_rs(&build_rs_path, &pkg_name, &spec)?;
    63→        }
    64→
    65→        let mut cmd = Command::new("cargo");
    66→        if requires_nightly(&spec) {
    67→            cmd.arg("+nightly");
    68→        }
    69→        cmd.arg("test");
    70→        cmd.arg("-p").arg(pkg_name);
    71→        cmd.current_dir(&workspace);
    72→
    73→        // Set spec path for tspec-build library to read in build.rs
    74→        cmd.env("TSPEC_SPEC_FILE", path.as_os_str());
    75→
    76→        apply_spec_to_command(
    77→            &mut cmd,
    78→            &spec,
    79→            &workspace,
    80→            cli_profile,
    81→            expanded_td.as_deref(),
    82→        )?;
    83→        cmd.status().context("failed to run cargo test")?
    84→    } else {
    85→        println!("Testing {} (no tspec)", pkg_name);
    86→        let mut cmd = Command::new("cargo");
    87→        cmd.arg("test");
    88→        cmd.arg("-p").arg(pkg_name);
    89→        cmd.current_dir(&workspace);

    93→                _ => {
    94→                    cmd.arg("--profile").arg(p);
    95→                }
    96→            }
    97→        }
    98→        cmd.status().context("failed to run cargo test")?
    99→    };
   100→

   106→    if !status.success() {

    13→/// Build package(s) with a translation spec
    14→#[derive(Args)]
    15→pub struct BuildCmd {
    16→    /// Package to build (name or path, e.g. "." for current dir)
    17→    #[arg(value_name = "PACKAGE")]
    18→    pub positional: Option<String>,
    19→    /// Package to build (defaults to current directory or all packages)
    20→    #[arg(short = 'p', long = "package")]
    21→    pub package: Option<String>,
    22→    /// Build all workspace packages (even when in a package directory)
    23→    #[arg(short = 'w', long = "workspace")]
    24→    pub workspace: bool,
    25→    /// Spec file(s) or glob pattern(s) to build with (defaults to package's tspec file)
    26→    #[arg(short = 't', long = "tspec", num_args = 1..)]
    27→    pub tspec: Vec<String>,
    28→    /// Release build
    29→    #[arg(short, long, conflicts_with = "profile")]
    30→    pub release: bool,
    31→    /// Build profile (e.g., release, release-small, or any custom profile)
    32→    #[arg(long)]
    33→    pub profile: Option<String>,
    34→    /// Strip symbols from binary after build
    35→    #[arg(short, long)]
    36→    pub strip: bool,
    37→    /// Stop on first failure (for all-packages mode)
    38→    #[arg(short, long)]
    39→    pub fail_fast: bool,
    40→}
    41→
    42→impl BuildCmd {
    43→    /// Resolve the effective profile from --release / --profile flags.
    44→    fn effective_profile(&self) -> Option<&str> {
    45→        if let Some(ref p) = self.profile {
    46→            Some(p)
    47→        } else if self.release {
    48→            Some("release")
    49→        } else {
    50→            None
    51→        }
    52→    }
    53→}
    54→
    55→impl Execute for BuildCmd {
    56→    fn execute(&self, project_root: &Path) -> Result<ExitCode> {
    57→        let cli_profile = self.effective_profile();
    58→
    59→        // Resolve package: --workspace > -p/positional PKG > cwd > all
    60→        let resolved = if self.workspace {
    61→            None
    62→        } else {
    63→            match self.positional.as_deref().or(self.package.as_deref()) {
    64→                Some(pkg) => resolve_package_arg(pkg)?,
    65→                None => current_package_name(),
    66→            }
    67→        };
    68→
    69→        match resolved {
    70→            None => {
    71→                if !self.tspec.is_empty() {
    72→                    anyhow::bail!(
    73→                        "-t/--tspec cannot be used in all-packages mode. Each package uses its own tspecs."
    74→                    );
    75→                }
    76→                let workspace = WorkspaceInfo::discover()?;
    77→                let results = build_all(&workspace, None, cli_profile, self.strip, self.fail_fast);
    78→                Ok(print_summary(&results))
    79→            }
    80→            Some(name) => {
    81→                if self.tspec.is_empty() {
    82→                    let result = build_package(&name, None, cli_profile)?;
    83→                    if self.strip {
    84→                        strip_binary(&result.binary_path)?;
    85→                    }
    86→                } else {
    87→                    let package_dir = resolve_package_dir(project_root, Some(&name))?;
    88→                    let pkg_name = get_package_name(&package_dir)?;
    89→                    let spec_paths = find_tspecs(&package_dir, &self.tspec)?;
    90→                    for spec_path in &spec_paths {
    91→                        let spec_str = spec_path.to_string_lossy();
    92→                        let result = build_package(&pkg_name, Some(&spec_str), cli_profile)?;
    93→                        if self.strip {
    94→                            strip_binary(&result.binary_path)?;
    95→                        }
    96→                    }
    97→                }
    98→                Ok(ExitCode::SUCCESS)
    99→            }
   100→        }
   101→    }
   102→}

+/// Built-in cargo profiles that don't require a `[profile.<name>]` definition.
+const BUILTIN_PROFILES: &[&str] = &["dev", "debug", "release", "test", "bench"];
+
+/// Validate that a custom profile is defined in the workspace Cargo.toml.
+/// Built-in profiles (dev, release, test, bench) are always valid.
+/// Custom profiles must have a `[profile.<name>]` section with `inherits`.
+pub fn validate_profile(profile: &str, workspace: &Path) -> Result<()> {
+    if BUILTIN_PROFILES.contains(&profile) {
+        return Ok(());
+    }
+    let cargo_toml_path = workspace.join("Cargo.toml");
+    let content = fs::read_to_string(&cargo_toml_path)
+        .with_context(|| format!("failed to read {}", cargo_toml_path.display()))?;
+    let doc: toml::Value =
+        toml::from_str(&content).context("failed to parse workspace Cargo.toml")?;
+    if let Some(profiles) = doc.get("profile").and_then(|p| p.as_table())
+        && profiles.contains_key(profile)
+    {
+        return Ok(());
+    }
+    bail!(
+        "profile `{}` is not defined in {}. Custom profiles must be defined with \
+         `[profile.{}]` and an `inherits` field (e.g., `inherits = \"release\"`).",
+        profile,
+        cargo_toml_path.display(),
+        profile,
+    )
+}

   225→## 20260218 - Add custom profile support
   226→
   227→### Context
   228→
   229→Currently `cargo.profile` only accepts `"debug"` or `"release"` (a Rust enum). Cargo supports
   230→custom profiles defined in `Cargo.toml` (e.g., `[profile.release-small]` with `inherits = "release"`),
   231→selected via `cargo build --profile <name>`. tspec should support selecting and overriding these
   232→custom profiles.
   233→
   234→Key insight: Custom profile **definitions** must live in `Cargo.toml` (cargo requirement — they
   235→need `inherits`). tspec's role is **selecting** a profile and **overriding** its settings via
   236→`cargo.config`.
   237→
   238→Cargo's profile-to-directory mapping: `dev` → `target/debug/`, `release` → `target/release/`,
   239→custom → `target/<name>/`.
   240→
   241→### Plan
   242→
   243→Multi-step (`-devN` series), version `0.12.0`.
   244→
   245→**Step 1 (dev1):** Core type change — replace `Profile` enum with `String`, update command
   246→generation (`"debug"`/`"dev"` → no flag, anything else → `--profile <name>`), update path
   247→resolution (`profile_dir_name()` helper), relax validation.
   248→
   249→**Step 2 (dev2):** CLI `--profile <name>` flag on build/run/test commands, thread through
   250→call chain, replace `release: bool` with `Option<String>`.
   251→
   252→**Step 3:** Final release — remove `-dev` suffix.
   253→
   254→### Changes
   255→
   256→**Step 1 (dev1):** Replaced `enum Profile { Debug, Release }` with `Option<String>`.
   257→Updated `apply_spec_to_command()` to emit `--profile <name>` for any non-debug/dev profile.
   258→Added `profile_dir_name()` helper for `dev` → `debug` directory mapping.
   259→Removed `validate_config_profiles()` — custom profiles in `[cargo.config]` are now accepted.
   260→Relaxed `validate_value("cargo.profile", ...)` to accept any string.
   261→
   262→**Step 2 (dev2):** Added `--profile <name>` flag to build/run/test commands (`conflicts_with = "release"`).
   263→Replaced `release: bool` with `cli_profile: Option<&str>` throughout the call chain:
   264→`build_package()`, `test_package()`, `apply_spec_to_command()`, `get_binary_path()`,
   265→`get_binary_path_simple()`, `build_all()`, `test_all()`, `run_all()`.
   266→Simplified `plain_cargo_build_release()` to a thin wrapper: `build_package(name, None, Some("release"))`.
   267→
   268→### Status
   269→
   270→Done — released in v0.12.0.
   271→

     1→//! High-level build options that expand to lower-level flags.

     3→//! These provide "easy generality" - user picks intent, implementation

     6→use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

     8→/// Panic handling strategy.
     9→///
    10→/// This is a high-level option that automatically sets the appropriate

    12→#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
    13→#[serde(rename_all = "kebab-case")]
    14→pub enum PanicMode {
    15→    /// Default Rust behavior - panic unwinds the stack.
    16→    #[default]
    17→    Unwind,
    18→
    19→    /// Panic aborts immediately (no unwinding).
    20→    /// Sets: rustc -C panic=abort
    21→    Abort,
    22→
    23→    /// Panic aborts with no formatting overhead (nightly only).
    24→    /// Sets: cargo -Z panic-immediate-abort AND rustc -C panic=immediate-abort
    25→    /// This eliminates all panic formatting machinery for smallest binaries.
    26→    ImmediateAbort,
    27→}

> AGENT

This is a small fix — single step, straight to v0.12.1. The spec has `panic = "abort"` which sets `-C panic=abort` via RUSTFLAGS. That's fine for builds, but `cargo test` needs `-Zpanic_abort_tests` (nightly) to compile tests with panic=abort.

The fix goes in `testing.rs`: detect abort-like panic modes, force nightly, and add `-Zpanic_abort_tests`.

> TOOL

  "old_string": "/// Check if spec requires nightly toolchain\nfn requires_nightly(spec: &crate::types::Spec) -> bool {\n    // High-level panic mode may require nightly\n    let panic_needs_nightly = spec.panic.map(|p| p.requires_nightly()).unwrap_or(false);\n\n    let has_build_std = !spec.cargo.build_std.is_empty();\n\n    let has_unstable = !spec.cargo.unstable.is_empty();\n\n    panic_needs_nightly || has_build_std || has_unstable\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Check if spec requires nightly toolchain for testing.\n/// This is stricter than the build version: panic=abort also needs nightly\n/// because `-Zpanic_abort_tests` is a nightly-only flag.\nfn requires_nightly_for_test(spec: &crate::types::Spec) -> bool {\n    let panic_needs_nightly = spec\n        .panic\n        .map(|p| p.rustc_panic_value().is_some()) // any non-unwind panic needs nightly for tests\n        .unwrap_or(false);\n\n    let has_build_std = !spec.cargo.build_std.is_empty();\n\n    let has_unstable = !spec.cargo.unstable.is_empty();\n\n    panic_needs_nightly || has_build_std || has_unstable\n}\n\n/// Check if spec uses an abort-like panic mode that needs `-Zpanic_abort_tests` for testing.\nfn needs_panic_abort_tests(spec: &crate::types::Spec) -> bool {\n    spec.panic\n        .map(|p| p.rustc_panic_value().is_some()) // abort or immediate-abort\n        .unwrap_or(false)\n}"
}

> AGENT

It's a rustc flag, not a cargo `-Z` flag. The error even says: "If you intended to use an unstable rustc feature, try setting `RUSTFLAGS="-Zpanic_abort_tests"`". It needs to go in RUSTFLAGS, not as a cargo argument.

Looking at the code, `apply_spec_to_command` already collects rustc flags into RUSTFLAGS. The cleanest fix is to add it there. But `apply_spec_to_command` is shared between build and test — I should add it only for test. Let me put it directly in the RUSTFLAGS env var in testing.rs:

> TOOL

> AGENT

It's not crashing on exit — it's the **bin test binary** segfaulting on startup. Two separate test binaries run:

1. `src/lib.rs` tests — 255 pass (this is a lib target, no `-static` flag)
2. `src/main.rs` tests — segfaults immediately

The spec has `linker.args = ["-static"]`, and `generate_build_rs` emits `cargo:rustc-link-arg-bin=tspec=-static` which applies only to bin targets. So the bin test binary gets statically linked with glibc, and glibc + `-static` = segfault. That's the known issue in your todo.

The lib test binary doesn't get `-static` (it's not a bin target), so it runs fine.

> DEVELOPER

So that's the user misconfiguring?

> AGENT

Yes — `-static` with glibc is fundamentally broken (glibc uses dlopen internally for NSS, iconv, etc.). The spec is asking for something that can't work on a glibc system. The correct fix is to use musl for static builds, which is already noted in your todo.

tspec could warn about this combination, but it's really a linker/libc constraint, not a tspec bug.

The package that failed is actually `tspec`, not `tspec-build` — you ran `tspec test -p tspec -t tspec.other.ts.toml`. The segfault is in the `tspec` binary test target (src/main.rs) because the `-static` linker flag from tspec-build's generated build.rs applies to the tspec bin target.

The error message `cargo test failed for 'tspec' with spec tspec.other.ts.toml` is correct — it's the `tspec` package that failed. Were you perhaps thinking of a different scenario, like running `tspec test` without `-p` where both packages run?

> AGENT

Right — you were right the first time, and now you can see both cases work:

- `tspec test -p tspec` → `Error: cargo test failed for 'tspec' with spec tspec.other.ts.toml`
- `tspec test -p tspec-build` → `Error: cargo test failed for 'tspec-build' with spec tspec.other.ts.toml`

The package name is correct in both. The tspec-build error is a different issue — it's a lib crate so `cargo:rustc-link-arg-bin` is invalid (no bin target). That's also a user misconfiguration — the spec's `linker.args` only makes sense for packages with a binary target.

Ready to commit?

{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/tspec/src/cargo_build.rs",
  "old_string": "/// Warn about spec settings that are likely misconfigurations.\npub fn warn_spec_misconfigurations(pkg_name: &str, spec: &Spec, pkg_dir: &Path) {\n    let has_linker_args = !spec.linker.args.is_empty();\n    let has_bin_target = pkg_dir.join(\"src/main.rs\").exists();\n\n    // -static with non-musl target (glibc + -static segfaults)\n    if has_linker_args {\n        let has_static = spec.linker.args.iter().any(|a| a == \"-static\");\n        let is_musl = spec\n            .cargo\n            .target_triple\n            .as_ref()\n            .is_some_and(|t| t.contains(\"musl\"));\n        if has_static && !is_musl {\n            println!(\n                \"Warning: -static linker arg without musl target for {}. \\\n                 glibc + -static often segfaults; consider using a musl target triple.\",\n                pkg_name\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    // linker.args on lib-only package\n    if has_linker_args && !has_bin_target {\n        println!(\n            \"Warning: linker.args ignored for {} (no binary target)\",\n            pkg_name\n        );\n    }\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Check for spec settings that are likely misconfigurations.\n/// Returns a list of warning messages (printed at top and bottom of output).\npub fn check_spec_misconfigurations(pkg_name: &str, spec: &Spec, pkg_dir: &Path) -> Vec<String> {\n    let mut warnings = Vec::new();\n    let has_linker_args = !spec.linker.args.is_empty();\n    let has_bin_target = pkg_dir.join(\"src/main.rs\").exists();\n\n    // -static with non-musl target (glibc + -static segfaults)\n    if has_linker_args {\n        let has_static = spec.linker.args.iter().any(|a| a == \"-static\");\n        let is_musl = spec\n            .cargo\n            .target_triple\n            .as_ref()\n            .is_some_and(|t| t.contains(\"musl\"));\n        if has_static && !is_musl {\n            warnings.push(format!(\n                \"Warning: -static linker arg without musl target for {}. \\\n                 glibc + -static often segfaults; consider using a musl target triple.\",\n                pkg_name\n            ));\n        }\n    }\n\n    // linker.args on lib-only package\n    if has_linker_args && !has_bin_target {\n        warnings.push(format!(\n            \"Warning: linker.args ignored for {} (no binary target)\",\n            pkg_name\n        ));\n    }\n\n    for w in &warnings {\n        println!(\"{}\", w);\n    }\n    warnings\n}\n\n/// Print collected warnings again so they're visible after cargo output.\npub fn reprint_warnings(warnings: &[String]) {\n    for w in warnings {\n        println!(\"{}\", w);\n    }\n}"
}

Excellent. Now I have all the information needed. Let me create a comprehensive report.

## Thorough Analysis: `-t` Glob Handling and Package Resolution

I've reviewed all the relevant code. Here's what I found:

### Key Finding: The Root Cause

**The problem is in the package resolution logic, not in the glob handling itself.** When `tspec build -t tspec*` is run without an explicit package argument, the command resolves to "all-packages mode" (because `current_package_name()` returns `None` at a workspace root), which then rejects `-t` with the error message.

---

### Package Resolution Logic (src/cmd/mod.rs, lines 38-76)

```rust
pub(crate) fn current_package_name() -> Option<String> {
    let cwd = std::env::current_dir().ok()?;
    // At a workspace root, don't treat it as a single package
    if cwd.join("Cargo.toml").exists() && !is_pop(&cwd) {
        return None;  // <-- WORKSPACE ROOT RETURNS NONE
    }
    get_package_name(&cwd).ok()
}

pub(crate) fn resolve_package_arg(pkg: &str) -> Result<Option<String>> {
    let workspace = find_project_root()?;
    let pkg_dir = find_package_dir(&workspace, pkg)?;
    match get_package_name(&pkg_dir) {
        Ok(name) => Ok(Some(name)),
        Err(_) => Ok(None),  // <-- Returns None if no package found
    }
}
```

**Key insight**: Both functions return `Option<String>`:
- `Some(name)` = single package mode
- `None` = all-packages mode

The tspec repository has **both `[workspace]` and `[package]`** (lines 1-8 of Cargo.toml). The `is_pop()` check (in `find_paths.rs`, line 76-85) explicitly treats this as a workspace, not a POP:

```rust
pub fn is_pop(project_root: &Path) -> bool {
    let cargo_toml = project_root.join("Cargo.toml");
    if let Ok(content) = std::fs::read_to_string(&cargo_toml) {
        // POP has [package] but no [workspace]
        has_toml_section_exact(&content, "package")
            && !has_toml_section_exact(&content, "workspace")  // <-- FALSE here
    } else {
        false
    }
}
```

---

### Command Resolution Flow (All 4 commands use identical pattern)

**src/cmd/build.rs lines 56-101:**

```rust
fn execute(&self, project_root: &Path) -> Result<ExitCode> {
    let resolved = if self.workspace {
        None
    } else {
        match self.positional.as_deref().or(self.package.as_deref()) {
            Some(pkg) => resolve_package_arg(pkg)?,
            None => current_package_name(),  // <-- THIS RETURNS NONE AT WORKSPACE ROOT
        }
    };

    match resolved {
        None => {
            if !self.tspec.is_empty() {
                anyhow::bail!(
                    "-t/--tspec cannot be used in all-packages mode. Each package uses its own tspecs."
                );  // <-- HITS THIS ERROR
            }
            // proceed with all-packages mode
        }
        Some(name) => {
            // single-package mode
            if self.tspec.is_empty() {
                // use default tspec
            } else {
                let spec_paths = find_tspecs(&package_dir, &self.tspec)?;  // <-- GLOB HANDLING HERE
            }
        }
    }
}
```

All four commands (**build**, **run**, **test**, **compare**) use the same pattern, lines 54-62.

---

### Glob Handling: `find_tspecs()` (src/find_paths.rs, lines 202-261)

The glob function itself is sophisticated and works correctly:

```rust
pub fn find_tspecs(pkg_dir: &Path, patterns: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>> {
    let default_pattern = format!("tspec*{}", TSPEC_SUFFIX);
    let patterns: Vec<&str> = if patterns.is_empty() {
        vec![&default_pattern]  // <-- FALLBACK TO tspec*.ts.toml IF NO PATTERNS
    } else {
        patterns.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect()
    };

    let mut results = Vec::new();

    for pattern in &patterns {
        // Try as literal path first (relative to cwd or absolute)
        let as_path = PathBuf::from(pattern);
        if as_path.exists() && as_path.is_file() {
            results.push(as_path.canonicalize().unwrap_or(as_path));
            continue;
        }

        // Try as literal path relative to pkg_dir
        let in_pkg = pkg_dir.join(pattern);
        if in_pkg.exists() && in_pkg.is_file() {
            results.push(in_pkg);
            continue;
        }

        // Try as glob pattern in pkg_dir
        let glob_pattern = Pattern::new(pattern)...?;
        let entries: Vec<_> = std::fs::read_dir(pkg_dir)?
            .filter_map(|e| e.ok())
            .filter(|e| {
                let name = e.file_name().to_string_lossy().to_string();
                e.path().is_file() && glob_pattern.matches(&name)
            })
            .map(|e| e.path())
            .collect();
        
        results.extend(entries);
    }

    // Remove duplicates and sort
    results.sort();
    results.dedup();
    
    Ok(results)
}
```

This function only runs when `resolved` is `Some(name)` (single-package mode). It's never called in all-packages mode.

---

### Why Compare "Works" (It Actually Also Fails)

**src/cmd/compare.rs lines 44-67:**

Compare has an **identical** rejection check at lines 46-49, and it will fail with the same error. However, compare has a subtle difference at line 59:

```rust
let spec_paths = if self.tspec.is_empty() {
    find_tspecs(&package_dir, &self.tspec).unwrap_or_default()  // <-- UNWRAP_OR_DEFAULT
} else {
    find_tspecs(&package_dir, &self.tspec)?  // <-- Propagate error
};
```

This doesn't actually help because:
1. Compare still rejects `-t` in all-packages mode (line 46-49)
2. The `unwrap_or_default()` only applies when `-t` is **empty**

Compare does NOT work better than build/run/test. All four commands have the same package resolution logic.

---

### The Real Issue: Package Argument Inference

The problem is that **there is no way to pass a package argument when using `-t`** without being explicit.

Looking at the resolution order (line 63 in build.rs):

```rust
match self.positional.as_deref().or(self.package.as_deref()) {
    Some(pkg) => resolve_package_arg(pkg)?,
    None => current_package_name(),  // <-- If no -p and no positional, uses cwd
}
```

At the tspec workspace root:
- No positional argument → `None`
- No `-p` argument → `None`
- `current_package_name()` → Returns `None` (workspace root is not a package)
- Resolution → `None` = all-packages mode
- With `-t` → **ERROR**

**The fix requires explicit package targeting:**
- `tspec build -p tspec -t tspec*` (works)
- `tspec build tspec -t tspec*` (works with positional)
- `tspec build -t tspec*` (fails at workspace root)

---

### Summary of Findings

| Item | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| **`current_package_name()` at workspace root** | Returns `None` (all-packages mode) |
| **`resolve_package_arg(".")`** | Returns `Some("tspec")` when in workspace root with root package |
| **`find_tspecs()` function** | Works correctly, but only called in single-package mode |
| **`-t` rejection** | Happens before glob resolution, in all-packages mode |
| **All 4 commands** | Use identical package resolution logic |
| **Compare command** | Has same restriction as build/run/test |

The `-t/--tspec cannot be used in all-packages mode` error is intentional: tspec needs to know which package's directory to search for specs. Without an explicit package argument, it defaults to all-packages mode at a workspace root.

---

1. `/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/tspec/src/cmd/mod.rs` - `current_package_name()` and `resolve_package_arg()`
2. `/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/tspec/src/find_paths.rs` - `find_tspecs()` and `is_pop()`
3. `/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/tspec/src/cmd/build.rs` - build command execution (lines 56-101)
4. `/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/tspec/src/cmd/run.rs` - run command execution (lines 56-110)
5. `/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/tspec/src/cmd/test.rs` - test command execution (lines 51-91)
6. `/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/tspec/src/cmd/compare.rs` - compare command execution (lines 33-69)
7. `/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/tspec/Cargo.toml` - workspace structure verification

Right — confirmed that compare has the same issue. The root cause: at a workspace root with `[package]`, `current_package_name()` returns `None` (all-packages mode) because it's not a POP. When `-t` is specified, this triggers the rejection error.

The fix: when `-t` is specified and we'd otherwise be in all-packages mode, try resolving `.` as a package. This works at a workspace root with `[package]` (returns `Some("tspec")`), and still errors at a pure workspace root.

    68→/// Returns None at a workspace root so that commands default to all-packages mode.
    69→pub(crate) fn current_package_name() -> Option<String> {
    70→    let cwd = std::env::current_dir().ok()?;
    71→    // At a workspace root, don't treat it as a single package
    72→    if cwd.join("Cargo.toml").exists() && !is_pop(&cwd) {
    73→        return None;
    74→    }
    75→    get_package_name(&cwd).ok()
    76→}
    77→

    14→pub struct CompareCmd {

    18→    /// Package to compare (defaults to current directory)
    19→    #[arg(short = 'p', long = "package")]

    27→    /// Stop on first failure (for all-packages mode)

    29→    pub fail_fast: bool,
    30→}
    31→
    32→impl Execute for CompareCmd {
    33→    fn execute(&self, project_root: &Path) -> Result<ExitCode> {
    34→        // Resolve package: --workspace > -p/positional PKG > cwd > all
    35→        let resolved = if self.workspace {
    36→            None
    37→        } else {
    38→            match self.positional.as_deref().or(self.package.as_deref()) {
    39→                Some(pkg) => resolve_package_arg(pkg)?,
    40→                None => current_package_name(),

    47→                    anyhow::bail!(
    48→                        "-t/--tspec cannot be used in all-packages mode. Each package uses its own tspecs."
    49→                    );
    50→                }
    51→                let workspace = WorkspaceInfo::discover()?;
    52→                let results = compare_all(&workspace, self.fail_fast);
    53→                Ok(print_compare_summary(&results))

    56→                let package_dir = resolve_package_dir(project_root, Some(&pkg_name))?;
    57→                let pkg_name = get_package_name(&package_dir)?;

     1→//! Batch operations on all workspace packages
     2→//!
     3→//! Provides build_all, run_all, test_all for operating on all workspace members.
     4→

    17→/// Result of a batch operation on a single package
    18→pub struct OpResult {
    19→    pub name: String,
    20→    pub success: bool,
    21→    pub message: String,
    22→    pub size: Option<u64>,
    23→}
    24→
    25→/// Build all workspace packages (excluding build tools)
    26→pub fn build_all(
    27→    workspace: &WorkspaceInfo,
    28→    tspec: Option<&str>,
    29→    cli_profile: Option<&str>,
    30→    strip: bool,
    31→    fail_fast: bool,
    32→) -> Vec<OpResult> {
    33→    let mut results = Vec::new();
    34→
    35→    for member in workspace.buildable_members() {
    36→        println!("=== {} ===", member.name);
    37→
    38→        let result = match build_package(&member.name, tspec, cli_profile) {
    39→            Ok(build_result) => {
    40→                if strip
    41→                    && member.has_binary
    42→                    && let Err(e) = strip_binary(&build_result.binary_path)
    43→                {
    44→                    eprintln!("  warning: strip failed: {}", e);
    45→                }
    46→                let size = binary_size(&build_result.binary_path).ok();
    47→                OpResult {
    48→                    name: member.name.clone(),
    49→                    success: true,
    50→                    message: format!("{}", build_result.binary_path.display()),
    51→                    size,
    52→                }
    53→            }
    54→            Err(e) => OpResult {
    55→                name: member.name.clone(),
    56→                success: false,
    57→                message: e.to_string(),
    58→                size: None,
    59→            },
    60→        };
    61→
    62→        let failed = !result.success;
    63→        results.push(result);
    64→
    65→        if failed && fail_fast {
    66→            break;
    67→        }
    68→    }
    69→
    70→    results
    71→}
    72→
    73→/// Run all app packages sequentially
    74→pub fn run_all(
    75→    workspace: &WorkspaceInfo,
    76→    tspec: Option<&str>,
    77→    cli_profile: Option<&str>,
    78→    strip: bool,
    79→) -> Vec<OpResult> {
    80→    let mut results = Vec::new();
    81→
    82→    for member in workspace.runnable_members() {
    83→        println!("=== {} ===", member.name);
    84→
    85→        let result = match build_package(&member.name, tspec, cli_profile) {
    86→            Ok(build_result) => {
    87→                if strip && let Err(e) = strip_binary(&build_result.binary_path) {
    88→                    eprintln!("  warning: strip failed: {}", e);
    89→                }
    90→                match run_binary(&build_result.binary_path, &[]) {
    91→                    Ok(exit_code) => OpResult {
    92→                        name: member.name.clone(),
    93→                        success: true, // We don't treat non-zero exit as failure
    94→                        message: format!("exit code: {}", exit_code),
    95→                        size: None,
    96→                    },
    97→                    Err(e) => OpResult {
    98→                        name: member.name.clone(),
    99→                        success: false,
   100→                        message: format!("run failed: {}", e),
   101→                        size: None,
   102→                    },
   103→                }
   104→            }
   105→            Err(e) => OpResult {
   106→                name: member.name.clone(),
   107→                success: false,
   108→                message: format!("build failed: {}", e),
   109→                size: None,
   110→            },
   111→        };
   112→
   113→        results.push(result);
   114→    }
   115→
   116→    results
   117→}

   119→/// Test all workspace packages
   120→pub fn test_all(
   121→    workspace: &WorkspaceInfo,
   122→    tspec: Option<&str>,
   123→    cli_profile: Option<&str>,
   124→    fail_fast: bool,
   125→) -> Vec<OpResult> {
   126→    let mut results = Vec::new();
   127→
   128→    // Test regular packages (excluding Test kind which needs special handling)
   129→    for member in workspace.buildable_members() {
   130→        if member.kind == PackageKind::Test {
   131→            continue; // Handle test packages separately
   132→        }
   133→
   134→        println!("=== {} ===", member.name);
   135→
   136→        let result = match test_package(&member.name, tspec, cli_profile) {
   137→            Ok(()) => OpResult {
   138→                name: member.name.clone(),
   139→                success: true,
   140→                message: "ok".to_string(),
   141→                size: None,
   142→            },
   143→            Err(e) => OpResult {
   144→                name: member.name.clone(),
   145→                success: false,
   146→                message: e.to_string(),
   147→                size: None,
   148→            },
   149→        };
   150→
   151→        let failed = !result.success;
   152→        results.push(result);

   154→        if failed && fail_fast {

   156→        }
   157→    }
   158→
   159→    // Handle test packages (like rlibc-x2-tests) - build and run all test binaries
   160→    for member in workspace.test_members() {

   163→        // Build the test package (builds all binaries)
   164→        let build_result = match build_package(&member.name, tspec, cli_profile) {
   165→            Ok(r) => r,

   169→                    success: false,

   182→        let target_dir = build_result.target_base.join(profile_dir);

   185→        let test_binaries: Vec<_> = std::fs::read_dir(&target_dir)
   186→            .into_iter()

   188→            .filter_map(|e| e.ok())

   196→                    .unwrap_or(false);
   197→                is_file && is_test && is_executable
   198→            })
   199→            .collect();
   200→
   201→        if test_binaries.is_empty() {

   260→/// Print a summary of operation results (for tests)
   261→pub fn print_test_summary(results: &[OpResult]) -> ExitCode {
   262→    let max_name_len = results
   263→        .iter()
   264→        .map(|r| r.name.len())
   265→        .max()
   266→        .unwrap_or(5)
   267→        .max(5);
   268→
   269→    println!();
   270→    print_header!(format!("tspec {} TEST SUMMARY", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")));
   271→    println!("  {:width$}  Status", "Package", width = max_name_len);
   272→
   273→    let mut passed = 0;
   274→    let mut failed = 0;
   275→
   276→    for result in results {
   277→        let status = if result.success {
   278→            passed += 1;
   279→            "[PASS]"
   280→        } else {
   281→            failed += 1;
   282→            "[FAIL]"
   283→        };
   284→        println!("  {:width$}  {status}", result.name, width = max_name_len);
   285→    }
   286→
   287→    println!();
   288→    println!("  Test: {} passed, {} failed", passed, failed);
   289→    println!();
   290→    println!("  Note: Run `tspec test -p tspec` or `cargo test -p tspec` to test tspec itself");
   291→    print_hline!();
   292→    println!();
   293→
   294→    if failed > 0 {
   295→        ExitCode::from(1)
   296→    } else {
   297→        ExitCode::SUCCESS
   298→    }
   299→}
   300→
   301→/// Print a summary for build operations (OK/FAILED)
   302→pub fn print_summary(results: &[OpResult]) -> ExitCode {
   303→    let max_name_len = results
   304→        .iter()
   305→        .map(|r| r.name.len())
   306→        .max()
   307→        .unwrap_or(5)
   308→        .max(5);
   309→
   310→    println!();
   311→    print_header!("BUILD SUMMARY");
   312→    println!(
   313→        "  {:width$}  Status    Size",
   314→        "Package",
   315→        width = max_name_len
   316→    );
   317→
   318→    let mut ok_count = 0;
   319→    let mut failed_count = 0;
   320→
   321→    for result in results {
   322→        let status = if result.success {
   323→            ok_count += 1;
   324→            "[ OK ]"
   325→        } else {
   326→            failed_count += 1;
   327→            "[FAIL]"
   328→        };
   329→        let size_str = result
   330→            .size
   331→            .map(format_size)
   332→            .unwrap_or_else(|| "--".to_string());
   333→        println!(
   334→            "  {:width$}  {status}  {:>6}",
   335→            result.name,
   336→            size_str,
   337→            width = max_name_len
   338→        );
   339→    }
   340→
   341→    println!();
   342→    println!("  Build: {} ok, {} failed", ok_count, failed_count);
   343→    print_hline!();
   344→    println!();
   345→
   346→    if failed_count > 0 {
   347→        ExitCode::from(1)
   348→    } else {
   349→        ExitCode::SUCCESS
   350→    }
   351→}
   352→
   353→fn format_size(bytes: u64) -> String {
   354→    if bytes >= 1_000_000 {
   355→        format!("{:.1}M", bytes as f64 / 1_000_000.0)
   356→    } else if bytes >= 1_000 {
   357→        format!("{:.1}K", bytes as f64 / 1_000.0)
   358→    } else {
   359→        format!("{}", bytes)
   360→    }
   361→}
   362→
   363→/// Result of a compare operation on a single package
   364→pub struct CompareResult {
   365→    pub op: OpResult,
   366→    pub specs: Vec<SpecResult>,
   367→}
   368→
   369→/// Compare all workspace packages that have binaries
   370→pub fn compare_all(workspace: &WorkspaceInfo, fail_fast: bool) -> Vec<CompareResult> {
   371→    let mut results = Vec::new();
   372→
   373→    for member in workspace.buildable_members() {
   374→        if !member.has_binary {
   375→            continue;
   376→        }
   377→
   378→        let spec_paths = find_tspecs(&member.path, &[]).unwrap_or_default();
   379→
   380→        println!("=== {} ===", member.name);
   381→
   382→        let (op, specs) = match compare_specs(&member.name, &spec_paths) {
   383→            Ok(spec_results) => (
   384→                OpResult {
   385→                    name: member.name.clone(),
   386→                    success: true,
   387→                    message: "ok".to_string(),
   388→                    size: None,
   389→                },
   390→                spec_results,
   391→            ),
   392→            Err(e) => (
   393→                OpResult {
   394→                    name: member.name.clone(),
   395→                    success: false,
   396→                    message: e.to_string(),
   397→                    size: None,
   398→                },
   399→                Vec::new(),
   400→            ),
   401→        };
   402→
   403→        let failed = !op.success;
   404→        results.push(CompareResult { op, specs });
   405→
   406→        if failed && fail_fast {
   407→            break;
   408→        }
   409→    }
   410→
   411→    results
   412→}
   413→
   414→/// Print a summary for compare operations
   415→///
   416→/// With a single package, just prints its comparison table.
   417→/// With multiple packages, reprints all per-package tables then an overall OK/FAIL summary.
   418→pub fn print_compare_summary(results: &[CompareResult]) -> ExitCode {
   419→    let has_failure = results.iter().any(|r| !r.op.success);
   420→
   421→    // Reprint per-package comparison tables together
   422→    for result in results {
   423→        if !result.specs.is_empty() {
   424→            print_comparison(&result.op.name, &result.specs);
   425→        }
   426→    }
   427→
   428→    // Only show overall COMPARE SUMMARY when there are multiple packages
   429→    if results.len() > 1 {
   430→        let max_name_len = results
   431→            .iter()
   432→            .map(|r| r.op.name.len())
   433→            .max()
   434→            .unwrap_or(5)
   435→            .max(5);
   436→
   437→        print_header!("COMPARE SUMMARY");
   438→        println!("  {:width$}  Status", "Package", width = max_name_len);
   439→
   440→        let mut ok_count = 0;
   441→        let mut failed_count = 0;
   442→
   443→        for result in results {
   444→            let status = if result.op.success {
   445→                ok_count += 1;
   446→                "[ OK ]"
   447→            } else {
   448→                failed_count += 1;
   449→                "[FAIL]"
   450→            };
   451→            println!(
   452→                "  {:width$}  {status}",
   453→                result.op.name,
   454→                width = max_name_len
   455→            );
   456→        }
   457→
   458→        println!();
   459→        println!("  Compare: {} ok, {} failed", ok_count, failed_count);
   460→        print_hline!();
   461→        println!();
   462→    }
   463→
   464→    if has_failure {
   465→        ExitCode::from(1)
   466→    } else {
   467→        ExitCode::SUCCESS
   468→    }
   469→}
   470→
   471→/// Print a summary for run operations (shows exit codes, not pass/fail)
   472→pub fn print_run_summary(results: &[OpResult]) -> ExitCode {
   473→    let max_name_len = results
   474→        .iter()
   475→        .map(|r| r.name.len())
   476→        .max()
   477→        .unwrap_or(5)
   478→        .max(5);
   479→
   480→    println!();
   481→    print_header!("RUN SUMMARY");
   482→    println!("  {:width$}  Exit", "Package", width = max_name_len);
   483→
   484→    let mut error_count = 0;
   485→
   486→    for result in results {
   487→        if result.success {
   488→            // Extract exit code number from message "exit code: X"
   489→            let code = result
   490→                .message
   491→                .strip_prefix("exit code: ")
   492→                .unwrap_or(&result.message);
   493→            println!(
   494→                "  {:width$}  {:>4}",
   495→                result.name,
   496→                code,
   497→                width = max_name_len
   498→            );
   499→        } else {
   500→            error_count += 1;
   501→            println!(
   502→                "  {:width$}  ERROR: {}",
   503→                result.name,
   504→                result.message,
   505→                width = max_name_len
   506→            );
   507→        }
   508→    }
   509→
   510→    println!();
   511→    if error_count > 0 {
   512→        println!("  Run: {} error(s)", error_count);
   513→    }
   514→    print_hline!();
   515→    println!();
   516→
   517→    if error_count > 0 {
   518→        ExitCode::from(1)
   519→    } else {
   520→        ExitCode::SUCCESS
   521→    }
   522→}
   523→

    30→/// Trait for command execution.
    31→pub trait Execute {
    32→    fn execute(&self, project_root: &Path) -> Result<ExitCode>;
    33→}
    34→
    35→/// Resolve a `-p` argument (path or name) to the actual cargo package name.
    36→/// Returns Some(name) for a package, None if it resolves to a workspace root
    37→/// with no `[package]` section (meaning "operate on all packages").
    38→pub(crate) fn resolve_package_arg(pkg: &str) -> Result<Option<String>> {
    39→    let workspace = find_project_root()?;
    40→    let pkg_dir = find_package_dir(&workspace, pkg)?;
    41→    match get_package_name(&pkg_dir) {
    42→        Ok(name) => Ok(Some(name)),
    43→        Err(_) => Ok(None),
    44→    }
    45→}
    46→
    47→/// Helper for commands that execute a cargo subcommand.
    48→pub fn execute_cargo_subcommand(
    49→    subcommand: &str,
    50→    args: &[OsString],
    51→    project_root: &Path,
    52→) -> Result<ExitCode> {
    53→    let mut cmd = std::process::Command::new("cargo");
    54→    cmd.arg(subcommand);
    55→    cmd.args(args);
    56→    cmd.current_dir(project_root);
    57→    let status = cmd
    58→        .status()
    59→        .with_context(|| format!("failed to run cargo {}", subcommand))?;
    60→    if status.success() {
    61→        Ok(ExitCode::SUCCESS)
    62→    } else {
    63→        bail!("cargo {} failed", subcommand);
    64→    }
    65→}
    66→
    67→/// Check if current directory is a package (has Cargo.toml with [package]).
    68→/// Returns None at a workspace root so that commands default to all-packages mode.
    69→pub(crate) fn current_package_name() -> Option<String> {
    70→    let cwd = std::env::current_dir().ok()?;
    71→    // At a workspace root, don't treat it as a single package
    72→    if cwd.join("Cargo.toml").exists() && !is_pop(&cwd) {
    73→        return None;
    74→    }
    75→    get_package_name(&cwd).ok()
    76→}

  "new_string": "/// Build all workspace packages (excluding build tools)\n///\n/// When `tspec_patterns` is empty, each package uses its default spec.\n/// When non-empty, patterns are resolved per-package via `find_tspecs`;\n/// packages with no matching specs are skipped.\npub fn build_all(\n    workspace: &WorkspaceInfo,\n    tspec_patterns: &[String],\n    cli_profile: Option<&str>,\n    strip: bool,\n    fail_fast: bool,\n) -> Vec<OpResult> {\n    let mut results = Vec::new();\n\n    for member in workspace.buildable_members() {\n        println!(\"=== {} ===\", member.name);\n\n        let specs = resolve_specs_for_member(&member.path, tspec_patterns);\n        if specs.is_empty() && !tspec_patterns.is_empty() {\n            continue; // no matching specs for this package\n        }\n\n        let spec_list: Vec<Option<String>> = if specs.is_empty() {\n            vec![None] // default spec\n        } else {\n            specs\n                .into_iter()\n                .map(|p| Some(p.to_string_lossy().into_owned()))\n                .collect()\n        };\n\n        for tspec in &spec_list {\n            let result = match build_package(&member.name, tspec.as_deref(), cli_profile) {\n                Ok(build_result) => {\n                    if strip\n                        && member.has_binary\n                        && let Err(e) = strip_binary(&build_result.binary_path)\n                    {\n                        eprintln!(\"  warning: strip failed: {}\", e);\n                    }\n                    let size = binary_size(&build_result.binary_path).ok();\n                    OpResult {\n                        name: member.name.clone(),\n                        success: true,\n                        message: format!(\"{}\", build_result.binary_path.display()),\n                        size,\n                    }\n                }\n                Err(e) => OpResult {\n                    name: member.name.clone(),\n                    success: false,\n                    message: e.to_string(),\n                    size: None,\n                },\n            };\n\n            let failed = !result.success;\n            results.push(result);\n\n            if failed && fail_fast {\n                return results;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    results\n}"
}

  "new_string": "/// Run all app packages sequentially\n///\n/// When `tspec_patterns` is empty, each package uses its default spec.\n/// When non-empty, patterns are resolved per-package; packages with no matches are skipped.\npub fn run_all(\n    workspace: &WorkspaceInfo,\n    tspec_patterns: &[String],\n    cli_profile: Option<&str>,\n    strip: bool,\n) -> Vec<OpResult> {\n    let mut results = Vec::new();\n\n    for member in workspace.runnable_members() {\n        println!(\"=== {} ===\", member.name);\n\n        let specs = resolve_specs_for_member(&member.path, tspec_patterns);\n        if specs.is_empty() && !tspec_patterns.is_empty() {\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        let spec_list: Vec<Option<String>> = if specs.is_empty() {\n            vec![None]\n        } else {\n            specs\n                .into_iter()\n                .map(|p| Some(p.to_string_lossy().into_owned()))\n                .collect()\n        };\n\n        for tspec in &spec_list {\n            let result = match build_package(&member.name, tspec.as_deref(), cli_profile) {\n                Ok(build_result) => {\n                    if strip && let Err(e) = strip_binary(&build_result.binary_path) {\n                        eprintln!(\"  warning: strip failed: {}\", e);\n                    }\n                    match run_binary(&build_result.binary_path, &[]) {\n                        Ok(exit_code) => OpResult {\n                            name: member.name.clone(),\n                            success: true,\n                            message: format!(\"exit code: {}\", exit_code),\n                            size: None,\n                        },\n                        Err(e) => OpResult {\n                            name: member.name.clone(),\n                            success: false,\n                            message: format!(\"run failed: {}\", e),\n                            size: None,\n                        },\n                    }\n                }\n                Err(e) => OpResult {\n                    name: member.name.clone(),\n                    success: false,\n                    message: format!(\"build failed: {}\", e),\n                    size: None,\n                },\n            };\n\n            results.push(result);\n        }\n    }\n\n    results\n}"
}

In all-packages mode (pure workspace\nor `--workspace`), using `-t` bails with \"requires a package target\". The user wants `-t tspec*`\nto apply to all sub-packages in a workspace, resolving the glob per-package and skipping packages\nwith no matches.\n\n### Plan\n\n**Step 1 (v0.12.5-dev1):** Update `all.rs` batch functions\n- Add `resolve_specs_for_member()` helper that calls `find_tspecs` per package, returns empty vec on no match\n- Change `build_all`, `test_all`, `run_all` signatures from `tspec: Option<&str>` to `tspec_patterns: &[String]`\n- Add `tspec_patterns: &[String]` parameter to `compare_all`\n- When patterns are empty: current behavior (each package uses its default spec)\n- When patterns are non-empty: resolve per-package, skip packages with no matches\n\n**Step 2 (v0.12.5-dev2):** Update command files\n- Remove the `bail!` for `-t` in all-packages mode from build, run, test, compare commands\n- Pass `&self.tspec` to the `_all` functions\n- Remove the `resolve_package_arg(\".\")` fallback hack (no longer needed — all-packages mode handles `-t` natively)\n\n**Step 3 (v0.12.5):** Final release\n\n### Status\n\nIn progress."
}
